nodes.label: future promise
nodes.def: Concurrency pattern decoupling value computation from access; Future represents pending result, Promise provides completion mechanism; enables asynchronous composition.

nodes.label: hb acquire fence
nodes.def: A memory fence that provides acquire semantics, ensuring all loads and stores after the fence are not reordered before the fence itself is observed.

nodes.label: hb antisymmetry
nodes.def: The property that if A happens-before B and B happens-before A, then A and B are the same operation; ensures well-defined ordering.

nodes.label: hb causality order
nodes.def: The partial order constraint that ensures cause precedes effect across the program, preventing out-of-thin-air values.

nodes.label: hb coherence order
nodes.def: The total order of all writes to the same memory location that determines which write a subsequent read will observe.

nodes.label: hb dependency chain
nodes.def: An explicit or implicit dependency from one operation to another that strengthens happens-before ordering beyond simple synchronization.

nodes.label: hb interrupt visibility
nodes.def: The guaranteed visibility of operations completed before an interrupt or context switch to the handler executing after.

nodes.label: hb irreflexivity
nodes.def: The property that no operation can happen-before itself; prevents circular causality in the ordering relation.

nodes.label: hb modification order
nodes.def: For a single variable, the total order of all writes to that variable; writes to the same variable are totally ordered within a thread's view.

nodes.label: hb reads from
nodes.def: The relation connecting a read operation to the write operation whose value it observes; foundational to establishing inter-thread ordering.

nodes.label: hb release fence
nodes.def: A memory fence that provides release semantics, ensuring all loads and stores before the fence are visible before the fence itself is issued.

nodes.label: hb seq cst boundary
nodes.def: The demarcation point where sequentially consistent operations establish a total order that all threads observe identically.

nodes.label: hb synchronization order
nodes.def: A total order established by synchronization operations (locks, barriers, atomic ops) that defines the global ordering of synchronization actions across all threads.

nodes.label: hb thread join
nodes.def: The join operation on a thread; the last operation in that thread happens-before the join operation completes in the joining thread.

nodes.label: hb thread start
nodes.def: The launch point of a thread; the start operation happens-before the first operation executed in that thread.

nodes.label: instruction reordering

nodes.label: invalidate queue
nodes.def: Hardware queue holding pending invalidation requests for cache lines; entries must be drained before a core can ensure it has exclusive ownership of a cache line.

nodes.label: linearizability
nodes.def: Correctness criterion requiring each operation appear to execute atomically at some point between invocation and response; composable property essential for concurrent object speci

nodes.label: livelock
nodes.def: Failure where threads continuously respond to each other without making progress; distinguishable from deadlock by active state; often result of excessive collision avoidance.

nodes.label: load buffering
nodes.def: Phenomenon in weak memory models where a load may observe a store from a different thread that happens later in global order, enabling patterns impossible under SC.

nodes.label: load buffering allowed

nodes.label: load linked store conditional
nodes.def: Pair of instructions for software atomic operations: LL reads atomically, SC writes only if no intervening store occurred; used on ARM, PowerPC; avoids ABA problem inherent to CAS.

nodes.label: lock elision
nodes.def: Optimization technique using HTM or CAS to execute critical sections without holding the lock when no conflict occurs; combines performance of no-locking with safety of mutual excl

nodes.label: mcs lock fifo ordering
nodes.def: Property guaranteed by MCS queue structure; lock acquisition order matches the order of enqueue operations; provides fairness without centralized ticket counters.

nodes.label: mcs lock help links
nodes.def: Backoff resolution protocol during failed enqueue CAS; the thread that lost the CAS follows the discovered pointer chain to complete the linking work of the winner before retrying

nodes.label: mcs lock local spinning
nodes.def: Performance property of MCS; each waiter spins on its own thread-local qnode in its own cache line; eliminates cache-line ping-ponging between spinning threads; reduces bus traffic

nodes.label: mcs lock qnode locked
nodes.def: Boolean field in qnode; spinning thread reads this; set true on enqueue and cleared false by predecessor upon release; default true indicates lock not yet released.

nodes.label: mcs lock qnode next
nodes.def: Pointer field in qnode referencing successor qnode; null until predecessor links this node; spinning thread polls this to detect when it has been chained into the queue.

nodes.label: mcs lock tail
nodes.def: Atomic shared pointer to the last enqueued qnode; initialized null; updated via CAS during enqueue; represents the lock acquisition frontier.

nodes.label: memory order relaxed atomicity guarantee

nodes.label: memory order relaxed modification order
nodes.def: The per-variable constraint that each atomic variable still has a well-defined modification order agreed upon by all threads, even though relaxed operations on different variables

nodes.label: memory order relaxed no ordering constraints
nodes.def: The defining property that relaxed operations impose zero ordering constraints relative to any other operations on any memory location; no happens-before or synchronizes-with relat

nodes.label: memory order relaxed reordering freedom
nodes.def: The freedom to reorder relaxed operations across variable boundaries; a relaxed store may be reordered with respect to a relaxed load on a different variable, and loads may observe

nodes.label: memory order relaxed vs release
nodes.def: The ordering contrast where release_semantics prevents prior operations from being reordered after the release, while memory_order_relaxed permits all such reorderings with no barr

nodes.label: memory order relaxed vs seq cst
nodes.def: The ordering contrast where sequentially_consistent imposes a single global total order visible to all threads, while memory_order_relaxed has no global ordering requirement across

nodes.label: memory order release
nodes.def: Memory ordering barrier ensuring all loads and stores before the barrier in program order cannot be reordered after it, making prior writes visible to acquiring threads.

nodes.label: mutex livelock prevention
nodes.def: Techniques including exponential backoff, random delays, or lock registry to prevent threads from repeatedly colliding on lock acquisition.

nodes.label: no happens before establishment
nodes.def: A relaxed operation neither participates in nor establishes a happens-before relationship with any other operation; operations may be reordered arbitrarily across thread boundaries

nodes.label: no synchronizes with establishment
nodes.def: A relaxed operation cannot synchronize-with any operation on another thread; release semantics and acquire semantics are absent, breaking the synchronizes-with chain.

nodes.label: numa awareness
nodes.def: Design consideration for systems with non-uniform memory access latency; thread affinity and data placement affect performance; synchronization must account for remote vs local mem

nodes.label: obstruction free
nodes.def: Progress guarantee where a thread completes an operation if it runs alone without interference; may starve under contention but has no blocking operations.

nodes.label: partial store order pso
nodes.def: Memory model (SPARC) where stores may be reordered with respect to older stores but loads maintain program order relative to other loads and stores respect address dependencies; re

nodes.label: powerpc memory model
nodes.def: Weak memory model used by PowerPC/POWER processors with similar permissiveness to ARM; requires explicit barriers for many ordering guarantees.

nodes.label: priority inheritance
nodes.def: Protocol resolving priority inversion by temporarily elevating the priority of a lock-holding low-priority thread to match the highest blocked thread.

nodes.label: producer consumer
nodes.def: Concurrent pattern with producer threads generating work consumed by consumer threads; typically synchronized with bounded or unbounded channels/queues.

nodes.label: race condition
nodes.def: Behavior where program outcome depends on relative timing of interleaved operations on shared state; general term for any timing-dependent bug in concurrent programs.

nodes.label: rcu read copy update
nodes.def: Linux kernel synchronization mechanism allowing read-heavy workloads without reader locks; readers access data freely while writers make copies and schedule updates for later recla

nodes.label: recursive mutex
nodes.def: Mutex variant permitting the same thread to acquire the lock multiple times; must be released same number of times; can hide design problems but necessary in some recursive pattern

nodes.label: relaxed no ordering constraints vs acquire subsequent constrained
nodes.def: The scope contrast where relaxed operations impose zero ordering constraints on any other operations on any memory location, while acquire semantics constrains all subsequent loads

nodes.label: relaxed vs seq cst
nodes.def: Relaxed operations are not part of the single total order of sequentially consistent operations; they do not participate in the global synchronization order that sequentially consi

nodes.label: rlx atomic read
nodes.def: A relaxed atomic load reads the atomic variable as one indivisible step; other threads cannot observe a torn or partial value from this read operation.

nodes.label: rlx atomic write
nodes.def: A relaxed atomic store writes the atomic variable as one indivisible step; other threads cannot observe a torn or partial value from this write operation.

nodes.label: rlx lli sc provenance
nodes.def: Load-linked/store-conditional primitives or bus-snooping mechanisms provide the hardware-level indivisibility guarantee underlying software-level relaxed atomicity.

nodes.label: rlx no intermediate state
nodes.def: The guarantee that no intermediate write value or partial read result is observable by any thread during the execution of a relaxed atomic operation; the variable transitions direc

nodes.label: rlx per variable scope
nodes.def: The atomicity guarantee is scoped per individual atomic variable; relaxed atomicity on one variable does not impose or imply atomicity constraints on operations on any other variab

nodes.label: seq cst atomic visibility atomic read returns written value

nodes.label: seq cst atomic visibility most recent write in total order
nodes.def: A seq_cst load observes the value written by the most recent seq_cst store to the same address in the global total order; no later store in the order can be the source of the obser

nodes.label: seq cst atomic visibility no intermediate state visibility
nodes.def: During the execution of a seq_cst load or store, no intermediate memory state is visible to any thread; the operation is indivisible and appears instantaneous to all observers in t

nodes.label: seq cst atomic visibility total order observation point
nodes.def: The logical position in the seq_cst global total order at which a given sequentially consistent read operation observes the effects of preceding operations; the read's visible valu

nodes.label: seq cst default atomic ordering
nodes.def: The default memory ordering for std::atomic operations in C11/C++11 when no memory_order is explicitly specified; provides the strongest guarantees without requiring explicit fence

nodes.label: seq cst fence
nodes.def: The explicit memory fence with sequentially consistent ordering that provides both acquire and release semantics plus additional ordering constraints to enforce the global total or

nodes.label: seq cst program order preservation
nodes.def: Within each thread, sequentially consistent operations maintain program order; no reordering of these operations is permitted within the same thread.

nodes.label: serializability
nodes.def: Correctness criterion for transaction systems requiring equivalent to some serial execution of transactions; differs from linearizability in handling multiple operations per transa

nodes.label: speculative execution
nodes.def: CPU technique executing instructions before their need is confirmed (e.g., branch prediction); rolled back on misprediction; interacts with memory ordering when speculative loads s

nodes.label: starvation
nodes.def: Condition where a thread is perpetually denied resources needed for progress due to scheduling or contention patterns; unfair lock implementations may starve waiters.

nodes.label: store buffer
nodes.def: Hardware structure buffering stores before they become visible to other cores; essential for TSO performance but creates visibility delays requiring memory barriers to manage.

nodes.label: store buffer linger
nodes.def: A relaxed store may remain in a store buffer indefinitely before becoming visible to other threads; no fence or ordering constraint forces a flush.

nodes.label: sw acquire atomic read
nodes.def: An atomic read operation with acquire semantics that observes the value written by a release write from another thread, establishing the synchronization point.

nodes.label: sw inter thread happens before
nodes.def: The cross-thread ordering relation established when a release operation synchronizes with an acquire operation; all effects visible to the releasing thread become visible to the ac

nodes.label: sw program order
nodes.def: The ordering guarantee within each individual thread: release fence orders all prior operations; acquire fence orders all subsequent operations.

nodes.label: sw release atomic write
nodes.def: An atomic write operation with release semantics that makes its value visible to other threads such that a subsequent acquire read from another thread can observe it.

nodes.label: sw seq cst atomic op
nodes.def: A sequentially consistent atomic operation that acts as both a release and acquire fence, providing the strongest memory ordering guarantee and synchronizing with all other seq_cst

nodes.label: sw thread pair
nodes.def: Two distinct threads of execution where the first performs a release operation and the second performs an acquire operation on the same atomic variable or synchronization primitive

nodes.label: sw visible side effect
nodes.def: The observable state change written by the releasing thread that becomes visible to the acquiring thread at the synchronization point.

nodes.label: synchronizes with ordering effect
nodes.def: The transitive visibility guarantee created when a release operation synchronizes with an acquire: all reads before the acquire see all writes after the matching release.

nodes.label: test and set
nodes.def: Atomic operation setting a memory location to a value (typically 1) and returning its previous contents; basis for simple spinlock implementations.

nodes.label: thread local storage
nodes.def: Per-thread data storage allocating distinct instances to each thread; avoids synchronization for thread-private data; accessed efficiently without locking.

nodes.label: thundering herd fairness starvation
nodes.def: A degraded thread fairness condition where some members of the wait_set are repeatedly overtaken by newly arriving competitors, never acquiring the resource despite eligibility.

nodes.label: thundering herd jitter decorrelation
nodes.def: Application of jitter to retry delays using full_jitter, equal_jitter, or decorrelated_jitter to prevent synchronized re-attempts among awakened threads, breaking retry_coordinatio

nodes.label: thundering herd phased awakening
nodes.def: A staged wakeup strategy dividing waiters into cohorts awakened in sequence rather than simultaneously, damping the contention surge through temporal distribution.

nodes.label: thundering herd wake one semantics
nodes.def: A notification strategy where at most one waiter is awakened per signal, eliminating the surge by design; the canonical mitigation for thundering-herd in mutex and condition-variab

nodes.label: ticket lock
nodes.def: Fair lock implementation using atomic ticket counter where threads take a ticket number and spin-wait until their number is called; ensures FIFO ordering and prevents starvation.

nodes.label: volatile java
nodes.def: Java modifier ensuring visibility of writes across threads; provides acquire/release semantics on reads and writes; different from C++ volatile which lacks memory ordering guarante

nodes.label: wait free
nodes.def: Strongest progress guarantee requiring every thread to complete any operation in finite steps regardless of other thread interference; no starvation possible.

nodes.label: work stealing
nodes.def: Load balancing strategy where idle threads steal work from busy threads' queues; typical in fork-join frameworks like Java ForkJoinPool; reduces contention compared to work distrib

nodes.label: sync atomic store load
nodes.def: An atomic_store with release semantics on thread A synchronizes_with an atomic_load with acquire semantics on thread B, making the stored value and all preceding writes visible to

nodes.label: sync fence pair
nodes.def: A release fence on thread A and an acquire fence on thread B that together establish the synchronizes_with relation, making all writes by A visible to B at the synchronization poin

nodes.label: sync lock release acquire
nodes.def: A lock_release operation on thread A synchronizes_with a lock_acquire operation on thread B, establishing ordering of all prior operations on A before subsequent operations on B.

nodes.label: sync read guarantee
nodes.def: The guarantee that a load following an acquire operation sees either the synchronized value or any write that happened-before the releasing store.

nodes.label: sync seq cst fences
nodes.def: Sequentially consistent fences that provide bidirectional synchronization guarantees, establishing mutual happens-before order between the synchronizing threads.

nodes.label: sync visibility boundary
nodes.def: The precise point in execution where inter-thread visibility is guaranteed, marking the happens-before boundary between writing thread and reading thread.

nodes.label: sync write guarantee
nodes.def: The guarantee that all memory writes preceding a release operation become visible at the synchronization point to any thread performing a subsequent acquire.

nodes.label: volatile cpp
nodes.def: C++ qualifier historically used for optimization barriers; in modern C++ standard, only provides address volatility semantics, not memory ordering; use std::atomic instead.

nodes.label: wake all semantics
nodes.def: Blocking primitive behavior — e.g., pthread_cond_broadcast, SetEvent, or equivalent — that resumes all waiting threads rather than selecting one; the direct cause of the wake spike

nodes.label: wake latency spread
nodes.def: Metric: the distribution of acquisition latencies among threads woken simultaneously; wide spread indicates thundering herd while tight clustering indicates controlled awakening.

nodes.label: wake one semantics
nodes.def: Blocking primitive behavior that resumes exactly one selected waiter per wake event; the canonical counter-pattern to wake_all_semantics.

nodes.label: wake ratio
nodes.def: Metric: threads woken per successful acquisition; a thundering herd has wake_ratio >> 1, ideally 1.

nodes.label: wake spike
nodes.def: The acute moment of mass simultaneous thread wake-up from a blocking primitive; the event horizon of the thundering herd.

nodes.label: waste ratio
nodes.def: Metric: fraction of awakened threads that re-block without acquiring; directly measures the cost of a thundering herd episode.

nodes.label: work bag pattern
nodes.def: A mitigation where the producer deposits work items into a lock-free queue and only one consumer wakes; avoids notifying all waiters entirely.
